{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) as measured by Time-to-Target, Success rate, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "The dataset contains 76,655 trials across 8 mice after filtering, with substantial imbalance across stimulation paradigms: Combined dominates with 48,846 trials (63.7%), followed by ICMS Only (11,378 trials, 14.8%), Dim Visual Only (9,603 trials, 12.5%), Sham (3,505 trials, 4.6%), and Bright Visual Only (3,323 trials, 4.3%)",
    "Overall success rate across all paradigms is 72.95% (SD=0.44), with mean Time-to-Target of 2.81 seconds (SD=2.08)",
    "Path Efficiency shows high variability (mean=0.47, SD=0.47, max=29.82), suggesting some trials had highly inefficient trajectories",
    "Average Speed is relatively consistent across all trials (mean=12.50 units/s, SD=4.46)",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) averages 0.38 (SD=0.24), ranging from near-zero to 1.0, indicating substantial variation in directional stability of navigation paths"
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Sample size imbalance is extreme: Combined paradigm has 14.7× more trials than Bright Visual Only, limiting statistical power for between-paradigm comparisons",
    "The five-fold difference in trial counts between the largest (Combined) and smallest (Bright Visual Only, Sham) groups may introduce precision disparities in estimating paradigm-specific means",
    "Path Efficiency shows the highest coefficient of variation (SD/mean ≈ 0.98), suggesting this metric may discriminate paradigms most effectively if group differences exist",
    "Success rate binary variance (SD=0.44 near theoretical maximum of 0.5) indicates adequate dynamic range for detecting paradigm effects on task completion"
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "The Combined paradigm—integrating intracortical microstimulation (ICMS) with visual cues—was tested most extensively, suggesting it may represent the primary experimental condition of interest. The inclusion of single-modality conditions (ICMS Only, Dim/Bright Visual Only) and Sham enables dissociation of sensory and stimulation contributions to navigation performance. However, the severely unbalanced design (63.7% Combined vs. 4.3% Bright Visual Only) means any cross-paradigm inference must account for dramatically different precision levels. The high path efficiency variability and wide AD range suggest navigation strategies differ substantially across trials, potentially reflecting paradigm-specific sensorimotor integration demands.",
  "limitations": [
    "No paradigm-specific descriptive statistics are provided—only grand means across all paradigms—making direct group comparisons impossible from current artifacts",
    "Extreme sample size imbalance (ranging from 3,323 to 48,846 trials per paradigm) violates equal-variance assumptions for standard ANOVA and reduces effective power for smaller groups",
    "Single-mouse identifiers prevent assessment of whether paradigm effects are consistent across subjects or driven by individual mouse differences",
    "Temporal or learning effects cannot be evaluated; trials may be ordered non-randomly within paradigms",
    "Path Efficiency maximum of 29.82 suggests outlier contamination or calculation anomalies that may distort mean-based summaries",
    "No information on task difficulty, target distance, or trial sequence effects that could confound paradigm comparisons"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Compute paradigm-specific means and standard errors for all five response variables, followed by mixed-effects models with Mouse as random effect to account for between-subject variability. Given the severe imbalance, use weighted or robust regression approaches, or subsample the Combined condition to match smaller group sizes for fair comparison. Conduct post-hoc pairwise tests with Tukey or Bonferroni correction, prioritizing contrasts of Combined versus single-modality conditions to assess synergy. Examine Path Efficiency and AD distributions for outliers before parametric testing, and consider non-parametric alternatives given the observed distributional irregularities."
}
